questions.text: Which one of the following is FALSE?
questions.solution:
Nondeterministic PDAs are strictly more powerful than deterministic ones; e.g. even-length palindromes [latex]ww^R[/latex] need nondeterminism. So not every NPDA has an equivalent DPDA.

The other statements are true.

Answer: Every nondeterministic PDA can be converted to an equivalent deterministic PDA

Every NFA can be converted to an equivalent PDA.
Complement of every context-free language is recursive.

questions.text:
Given the following statements
S1 : Every context-sensitive language L is recursive
S2 : There exists a recursive language that is not context-sensitive
Which statements are true?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- S1: a linear bounded automaton for a CSL can be simulated with only finitely many configurations, so membership is decidable [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] every CSL is recursive True
- S2: CSLs are a proper subset of recursive languages; there are recursive languages that are not context-sensitive (by diagonalization) True

Answer: Both S1 and S2 are correct

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: Both S1 and S2 are not correct
Both S1 and S2 are correct

questions.text:
Let L(R) be the language represented by regular expression R. Let L(G) be the language generated by a context free grammar G. Let L (M) be the language accepted by a Turning machine M. Which of the following decision problems are undecidable ?

I. Given a regular expression R and a string w, is w[latex]\in [/latex]L(R)?
II. Given a context-free grammar G, L(G)=[latex]\phi[/latex]?
III. Given a context-free grammar G, is L(G)=[latex]\Sigma[/latex]* for some alphabet [latex]\Sigma[/latex]?
IV. Given a Turning machine M and a string w, is w[latex]\in[/latex]L(M)?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: membership for a regular expression: build the automaton [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- II: emptiness of a CFG: check if S can generate a terminal string [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] decidable.
- III: is L(G) = [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] for a CFG [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.
- IV: TM membership (halting-like) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] undecidable.

Answer: III and IV only

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following languages

[latex]L_{1}=\{a^{p}|p[/latex] is a prime number}
[latex]L_{2}=\{a^{n}b^{m}c^{2m}|n\geq 0,m\geq 0\} [/latex]
[latex]L_{3}=\{a^{n}b^{n}c^{2n}|n\geq 0\}[/latex]
[latex] L_{4}=\{a^{n}b^{n}|n\geq 1\}[/latex]

Which of the following are CORRECT ?

I.[latex]L_{1}[/latex] is context-free but not regular.
II. [latex]L_{2}[/latex] is not context-free.
III. [latex]L_{3}[/latex] is not context-free but recursive.
IV. [latex]L_{4}[/latex] is deterministic context-free.
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1[/latex] (prime lengths) is not even context-free False
- [latex]L_2=a^nb^mc^{2m}[/latex] is context-free (push 2 per b, pop per c) False
- [latex]L_3=a^nb^nc^{2n}[/latex] is not CFL but clearly decidable True
- [latex]L_4=a^nb^n[/latex] is a deterministic CFL True

Answer: III and IV only

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Let [latex]\delta[/latex] denote that transition function and [latex]\hat{\delta}[/latex] denote the extended transition function of the [latex]\epsilon[/latex]- NFA whose transition table is given below:

Then [latex]\hat{\delta}(q_{2},aba)[/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
Use [latex]\epsilon[/latex]-closures: closure(q2) = {q2, q0}.
- on a: q0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] closure {q1, q2, q0}
- on b: q1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q3, q0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] closure {q3, q0, q2}
- on a: q0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] q1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] closure {q1, q2, q0}

Answer: {q0, q1, q2}
